 Commentary: A debt of gratitude 
 By JAMES R. POPLAR III 
 Nov 6, 2026 
 19 hrs ago 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 WhatsApp 
 SMS 
 Email 
 James Poplar
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 WhatsApp 
 SMS 
 Email 
 Print 
 Copy article link 
 Save 
 This Veterans Day we pay homage to those who have fought our nations wars for over 250 years and continue to do so till today. Some raised their hands and volunteered while other were drafted to taking the solemn oath “to solemnly swear that I will support and defend the Constitution of the United States against all enemies, foreign and domestic …”
 I too took that oath and like many other veterans lived it daily for most of my adult life. Like many of my fellow veterans regardless of branch of length of service we endured common hardships — months spent away from family and home, pay and benefits not consistent with our civilian peers, and unfortunately for some we returned with the battle still raging in our minds.
 Care of our veterans has seen steady improvements brought about by recent reforms; however, there are many veterans and their families among us who do not have a place to live, lack sufficient resources for a healthy diet, and saddest of all take their own lives out of sheer desperation. The suicide rate for is over twice as high as approximately eighteen veterans take their lives every day.
 The Commonwealth of Virginia ranks only after California as the state with the highest number of veterans. For these veterans providing much needed care for veterans and their families can be a constant struggle. Although the Federal Veterans Administration meets certain basic needs such as health care and transition counseling if a veteran in Virginia has an emergent need such as food or rent that the VA cannot provide to whom do they turn for assistance?
 Virginia is one of the few states that has an independent Veterans Service Foundation which supports the interests of Veterans and families. The Foundation provides supplemental funding when federal and state resources are not available or insufficient to meet the needs of our Veterans. More information can be found at https://virginiaveteransservicesfoundation.org/ 
 As President Lincoln stated in 1865: “To care for him who shall have borne the battle and for his widow, and his orphan,” not only on Veterans Day but throughout the year please both honor and support our veterans not only with a “Thank you for your service” but more importantly by supporting those to whom you owe a debt of gratitude for the freedom you enjoy today.
 James R. Poplar III, of Quicksburg, proudly served with the U.S. government for over 40 years. He specialized in national security affairs at both Vanderbilt and the National Defense University.
